Then, Bloomberg TV & Radio Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee and Bloomberg Rates Reporter Michael MacKenzie react to the bond market's spike and what it sets up for September as investors brace for another Fed meeting. Plus, Voya Financial CEO Heather Lavallee explains the trends she is seeing in Gen Z saving for retirement more than any other generation. Finally, Amazon Web Services General Manager of Media, Entertainment, Games and Sports Samira Bakhtiar discusses how the company is pioneering AI in entertainment production and content creation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Zelenskyy Threatens to Shut Air Traffic Over Russia With Drones
title_cn: 泽伦斯基威胁用无人机关闭俄罗斯上空的空中交通
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines to avoid Russian airspace as he threatened to respond to Moscow’s escalating missile attacks by crowding its skies with drones.

title: House Republicans 'Very Optimistic' That Party Will Hold Control of Congress
title_cn: 众议院共和党人“非常乐观”，认为该党将控制国会
summary: Indiana Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman said that his party is feeling 'very optimistic' that they can retain control of both the House and the Senate in the midterms, but acknowledged that candidates have work to do on the campaign trail to make it happen. The congressman also discussed US strikes in Iran, saying that the Iranian regime is trying to drag the conflict out as long as possible.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Burnham Says Water Central to UK Plan for Public Control
title_cn: 伯纳姆表示水是英国公共控制计划的核心
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the water industry “stands as a leaking monument” to what he sees as the failure of decades of privatization in Britain, signaling he’s open to nationalizing the industry.

title: Kuwait Decree Allows Government to Borrow From Wealth Fund
title_cn: 科威特法令允许政府从财富基金借款
summary: Kuwait’s government has issued a decree allowing it to borrow from its $1 trillion-plus sovereign wealth fund in order to support state finances, as Gulf economies deal with the impact of the US-Iran war.
